# Plan production quality and product release

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before manufacturing or releasing a physical-product batch or material design change. A traceable accepted batch or documented hold with quality evidence and release authority.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Define the product configuration and acceptance criteria

agent-runnable


Record the approved design, bill of materials, intended use, tolerances and test requirements. Identify product-market requirements with qualified specialists and keep unresolved safety questions outside release authority.

- Sources: [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Approve the production and quality plan

human · human approval required


Engineering, quality and operations owners agree supplier controls, process checks, sampling, traceability and nonconformance handling. Confirm responsibility for tooling, changes and outsourced tests.

- Sources: [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Run the controlled production and inspections

human · human approval required


Qualified operators execute the approved process and record material lots, measurements and deviations. Segregate unaccepted output and preserve traceability instead of changing acceptance criteria after seeing results.

- Sources: [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Review deviations and authorize release

human · human approval required


The designated quality and product authorities evaluate test evidence, corrective actions and applicable approvals. Record accepted concessions or holds and keep unsafe or unapproved product out of customer delivery.

- Sources: [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Reconcile batch records and field feedback

agent-runnable


Retain the configuration, release evidence and distribution traceability. Monitor returns and safety reports and feed recurring problems into corrective action and product-safety response.

- Verify: A traceable accepted batch or documented hold with quality evidence and release authority.
- Sources: [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices)
